title: in-essentials, in-standards and in-session carry dated history that every session loads with their rules
body:
Raised from Laksa's dc node on hv's word (Laksa `hv/inbox.dc.md` 2026-10-11 16:40Z), under hv's standing word on instruction docs (16:24Z): "Apart from obvious hard rules, we should probably always err on the side of less is more with skills.md and claude.md etc."

**The defect.** These skills load at every session start and after every compact, and some of their paragraphs tell how a rule came about rather than state it. Paragraphs that are only history, by line: `in-session/SKILL.md` 75 ("It is extracted from this prose..."), 77 ("How it resolves the session_id..."), 79 ("This replaced an earlier design...") and "Why this exists" (100-102), 1,387 bytes; `in-essentials/SKILL.md` 77 ("STEP 3 SAID..."), 574 bytes. History is also woven into rule paragraphs: `in-essentials` 64 (the `verblock:` note) and `in-standards` 15-18 (the dated MODULES.md and DECISION_TREE.md dispositions). The whole-paragraph part is about 2 KB, roughly 650 tokens a load, and it loads twice a restart until issue 0592 lands.

**Outcome wanted.** Each skill states its rules and procedure once; the history and the reasons live in the docs or `git log` rather than in what loads at startup; no rule is lost (check that each rule survives, including a rule stated inside a paragraph that goes).

## Resolution

Fixed by ce873474a for 3.2.4: `in-session`, `in-essentials` and `in-standards` state their rules and procedure without the paragraphs of history, and every rule those paragraphs carried survives in what loads.
